searchText: Added an illustrative example, <@429719902363058177> Pinging clients to make sure this does not get lost. Reth: <@429719902363058177> Geth: <@402853454126776320> Erigon: <@425274498732916736> Nethermind: <@316280621783580673> , <@628018527470616606> Besu: <@1252939266871263294> ethrex: <@281967554572976128> Two keys things: 1. Is this change small enough that we can deploy it on devnet-8 without breaking it? 2. Do clients things we should make this change? pinging also <@755913785620824175>, <@577788234810130432> , <@892053833121923094> and <@199561711278227457> for visibility cc <@830368514225340436> too since he helped refactoring many of the functions affected by this proposal I think the biggest question that needs to be answered first is if we are ok breaking the invariant that gas goes down monotonically in a callframe. As mentioned in the PR, this could give awkward results for contracts that use gas diff before and after to estimate call gas usage As far as the change itself, it makes sense and should not super complicated imo. Would defer to the clients on that one though GAS is not monotonic in a frame already, e.g. GAS SSTORE GAS. In Osaka spec or current EIP-8037 spec? I guess one can also argue that the `before_gas; CALL; after_gas; diff` pattern is already kind of broken. It returns inconsistent results depending on if the reservoir was used at all i.e. it returns child frame’ `state_gas + execution gas` if no reservoir was used for state operations and `execution_gas` if only the reservoir was used for state operations (and all possible results in between) In the current 8037 spec. In Osaka it always goes down (storage refunds are only collected during execution, applied in the end of a tx) Yes, but this will like break real 4337 bundles: the diff will wrap and strange things will happen. Do we have any 8037→4337 impact analysis? Have we considered GAS being `regular_gas+state_gas`? ^ <@968526635735326741> Even if we do this, I don't think it solves the GAS-no-longer-monotonic issue as the culprit is state refunds happening in-line, isn't it? yes, you are right in principle 1. I think we’d need a prototype and to sync that node onto glammy8, if it can sync to head then i can coordinate the fix across all hosts without any issues GAS-CALL-GAS is already not monotonic if CALL fails

excerpts.author: gurukamath
excerpts.content: I think the biggest question that needs to be answered first is if we are ok breaking the invariant that gas goes down monotonically in a callframe. As mentioned in the PR, this could give awkward results for contracts that use gas diff before and after to estimate call gas usage

excerpts.author: gurukamath
excerpts.content: As far as the change itself, it makes sense and should not super complicated imo. Would defer to the clients on that one though

excerpts.author: chfast
excerpts.content: GAS is not monotonic in a frame already, e.g. GAS SSTORE GAS.

excerpts.author: marioevz
excerpts.content: In Osaka spec or current EIP-8037 spec?

excerpts.author: gurukamath
excerpts.content:
I guess one can also argue that the `before_gas; CALL; after_gas; diff` pattern is already kind of broken. 

It returns inconsistent results depending on if the reservoir was used at all i.e. it returns child frame’ `state_gas + execution gas` if no reservoir was used for state operations and `execution_gas` if only the reservoir was used for state operations (and all possible results in between)

excerpts.author: chfast
excerpts.content: In the current 8037 spec. In Osaka it always goes down (storage refunds are only collected during execution, applied in the end of a tx)

excerpts.author: chfast
excerpts.content: Yes, but this will like break real 4337 bundles: the diff will wrap and strange things will happen. Do we have any 8037→4337 impact analysis?

excerpts.author: marioevz
excerpts.content: Even if we do this, I don't think it solves the GAS-no-longer-monotonic issue as the culprit is state refunds happening in-line, isn't it?

excerpts.author: chfast
excerpts.content: yes, you are right in principle
